chunks: Sa'd narrated from Abu Ja'far, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:
I asked him about a man who doubted, after he had prostrated, that he had not bowed. He said: 'He continues in his prayer.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one doubts whether they bowed before prostrating during prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of 'stability upon certainty' (istishab) in Shia jurisprudence, ruling that a doubt occurring after the completion of a pillar (sajdah) does not invalidate the prayer. It highlights the Shia preference for continuity over reconstruction in cases of minor uncertainty, distinguishing it from doubts arising before the pillar is fully established. This ruling is foundational for understanding the detailed laws of *shakk* in daily prayers.
